title: Une infirmière de province  (A Provincial Nurse)

segments.t: In the screening room, Andrea and the producers review the film footage featuring Corinne. Corinne explains her role as a nurse and shares a deeply poignant hospital memory, moving the entire room and making Andrea proud. Let's listen to their conversation in French first.
Le premier montage du film est prêt.
Je joue le rôle d'une infirmière.
Vous avez soigné un vieux patient?
Oui, le vieux monsieur Cardette.
Il avait presque quatre-vingt-dix ans.
Il voulait seulement un peu parler.
Mais je manquais cruellement de temps.
Quand je suis revenue, il était mort.
Votre émotion a bouleversé la salle!
Claude Lelouch m'a proposé un film.
C'est un honneur immense pour vous!
Merci pour cette soirée totalement incroyable.
Merci pour tout ce courage, Corinne.
J'étais très fière d'être votre agent!
Let's examine the conversation line by line and explore the French expressions.
Le premier montage du film est prêt.
'The first cut of the film is ready.' Andrea presents the work-in-progress cut. The adjective 'ready' indicates readiness.
Je joue le rôle d'une infirmière.
'I play the role of a nurse.' Corinne describes her on-screen character. The verbal phrase 'play' means to play the part.
Vous avez soigné un vieux patient?
'You cared for an elderly patient?' Andrea asks about the touching hospital scene. The verb 'cared for' means to care for or treat medically.
Oui, le vieux monsieur Cardette.
'Yes, elderly Mr. Cardette.' Corinne remembers the specific patient fondly. The courtesy title 'mister' precedes the family name.
Il avait presque quatre-vingt-dix ans.
'He was nearly ninety years old.' Corinne mentions the patient's great age. The compound numeral 'quatre-vingt-dix' designates ninety.
Il voulait seulement un peu parler.
'He only wanted to talk a little.' Corinne evokes the patient's simple wish for company. The restrictive adverb 'seulement' emphasizes his humble request.
Mais je manquais cruellement de temps.
'But I was desperately short on time.' Corinne describes the relentless pace of nursing. The verb 'lacked' expresses lacking or being short of something.
Quand je suis revenue, il était mort.
'When I returned, he had died.' Corinne recounts the heartbreaking hospital truth. The past tense 'was' describes the tragic discovery.
Votre émotion a bouleversé la salle!
'Your emotion moved the entire room!' Andrea highlights how profoundly everyone reacted. The verb 'moved deeply' means to move deeply or overwhelm emotionally.
Claude Lelouch m'a proposé un film.
'Claude Lelouch offered me a film.' Corinne shares the thrilling news of a role offer. The compound past verb 'a propose' denotes a formal proposal.
C'est un honneur immense pour vous!
'It is an immense honor for you!' Andrea celebrates the prestigious recognition. The noun 'honor' denotes deep respect and prestige.
Merci pour cette soirée totalement incroyable.
'Thank you for this totally incredible evening.' Corinne expresses her warmth and gratitude. The adjective 'incredible' highlights the surreal, wondrous night.
Merci pour tout ce courage, Corinne.
'Thank you for all this courage, Corinne.' Andrea honors her composure under pressure. The noun 'courage' commends her bravery before the producers.
J'étais très fière d'être votre agent!

'I was very proud to be your agent!' Andrea closes with sincere professional pride. The adjective 'proud' indicates deep admiration and pride. Now let's listen to the complete discussion once more to reinforce the vocabulary.

Corinne's raw emotional honesty saves the day for ASK, turning a potential disaster into a triumphant celebration. For one unforgettable evening, a humble provincial nurse became the brightest star in Paris. Now let's listen to the scene one last time in French.
